extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for claiming the benefit/priority of earlier U.S. (35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c)) and foreign applications (35 U.S.C. 119) under 37 CFR 1.78 and 1.55, including deadlines, required papers, petitions for unintentionally delayed claims, translation requirements, and examiner processing guidance. Primarily addressed to examiners for use in Office actions and to applicants/agents for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for making benefit claim (U.S. utility/plant applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after November 29, 2000, the benefit claim of the prior application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) must be made during the pendency of the application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application. This time period is not extendable and failure to submit the reference within this time period is considered a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2). Noncompliance = deemed waiver; use examiner form language notifying applicant that the benefit claim was not entered and that petition is required. Applies only to utility/plant apps filed on/after Nov 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for making benefit claim (national-stage from international application)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a nonprovisional application which entered the national stage from an international application after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371, the benefit claim must be made within the later of: (1) four months from the date on which the national stage commenced under 37 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f); or (2) sixteen months from the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2)(ii) and (a)(5)(ii). Time period is not extendable. Noncompliance may be addressed by petition for unintentionally delayed claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for unintentionally delayed nonprovisional benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2) is not submitted within the required time period, a petition for an unintentionally delayed claim may be filed under 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3). The petition must be accompanied by: (A) the reference required to the prior application (unless previously submitted); (B) a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.17(t); and (C) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions (see MPEP §1002.02(b)). Include required papers and surcharge. Examiner may request further information where unintentionality is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for unintentionally delayed provisional benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78(a)(5) is not submitted within the required time period, a petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim may be filed under 37 CFR 1.78(a)(6) during the pendency of the nonprovisional application. The petition must be accompanied by: (A) the required reference to the prior provisional application (unless previously submitted); (B) a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.17(t); and (C) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 CFR 1.78(a)(6). Same procedural requirements and forwarding to Office of Petitions apply as for nonprovisional petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when benefit claim elsewhere was recognized on filing receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant includes a claim to the benefit of a prior application elsewhere in the application but not in the manner specified in 37 CFR 1.78(a) (e.g., in an unexecuted oath/declaration or transmittal letter), and the Office recognized the information as shown by its inclusion on a filing receipt, the Office will not require a petition and surcharge to correct the benefit claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must still submit the benefit claim in the manner specified by 37 CFR 1.78(a) (amendment to first sentence(s) of the specification or ADS) to have a proper claim. If the information was not recognized (absent on filing receipt), a petition and surcharge are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition/filing-receipt absence requires petition & surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: If a benefit claim is included elsewhere in the application but is not recognized by the Office (e.g., absent from filing receipt or located in unconventional locations like the body of the specification), the Office will require a petition and the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.17(t) to correct the benefit claim because the application will not have been scheduled for publication on the basis of such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes timely-submitted-but-misplaced claims that were recognized (no petition) vs. those not recognized (petition required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a benefit claim after the required time period (possible additional filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a benefit claim is added after the time period required by 37 CFR 1.78(a), a petition and the surcharge are required. In addition, to add a benefit claim it may be necessary for applicant to file, depending on status: (A) a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 if the application is under final rejection or has been allowed; (B) a reissue application or a request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 if the application has issued as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment or ADS filed after final rejection or allowance is not entered as of right and must comply with 37 CFR 1.116 or 1.312. Consider procedural posture before accepting late-added benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference cannot add new matter to establish benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference statement added after an application's filing date is not effective because no new matter can be added after filing (see 35 U.S.C. 132(a)). If an incorporation by reference statement of the prior application was not presented upon filing, an incorporation-by-reference inserted later will not make the claim proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Dart Indus. v. Banner. If benefit claim submitted after filing relies on an incorporation-by-reference that was not present at filing, the amendment is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting benefit claims (effects and treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may cancel their claim to priority by amending the specification or submitting a new ADS to delete references to prior applications. The examiner should consider whether any new prior art may now be available if a benefit claim is deleted. Amendments/ADS to delete a benefit claim after final rejection or action are treated under 37 CFR 1.116 (see MPEP §§714.12, 714.13); after allowance treated under 37 CFR 1.312 (see MPEP §714.16). Deletion will not delay publication unless recognized within nine weeks prior to projected publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation may be viewed as intentional waiver; if applicant later petitions to accept an unintentionally delayed claim to add benefit back, the Office may refuse if delay was not unintentional. No supplemental declaration necessary to delete claim via ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) deletion limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a continued prosecution application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), no amendment may delete the specific reference to a prior application assigned the same application number. A specific reference in the CPA to a prior application assigned the same application number should not be made in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction or entry of the data can be made by technical support staff; a new PALM bib-data sheet should be printed and placed in the file. See MPEP §§707.05 and 1302.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same inventor(s) requirement for claiming benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute requires that applications claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 be filed by an inventor or inventors named in the previously filed application or provisional. 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1) and (a)(4) require that each prior-filed application must name as an inventor at least one inventor named in the later-filed application and disclose the named inventor’s invention claimed in at least one claim of the later-filed application in the manner provided by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must verify inventor identity and disclosure linkage between applications when assessing entitlement to benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement for non-English provisional benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If benefit is being claimed to a provisional application filed in a language other than English, an English language translation of the provisional application and a statement that the translation is accurate are required to be filed in the provisional application (see 37 CFR 1.78(a)(5)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation and statement were not filed as required, applicant will be notified in the nonprovisional and given time to file them in the provisional; failure to timely reply will result in abandonment of the nonprovisional. Form paragraph 2.38 may be used to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application must be entitled to a filing date and fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application must be entitled to a filing date under the applicable 37 CFR 1.53 provisions and the basic filing fee must have been paid within the pendency of the prior application (see 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1)). For nonprovisional prior-filed applications see 1.53(b)/(d) and 1.16; for provisional see 1.53(c) and the filing fee timing of 1.53(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application was not entitled to a filing date or did not include the basic filing fee, the present application is not entitled to the benefit and applicant must delete the reference. Form paragraph 2.40 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph / examiner notice for untimely benefit claim (¶ 2.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 2.39 notifies applicant that a benefit claim was not entered because the required reference was not timely filed within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2) or (a)(5) and instructs on petition procedure: file petition for unintentionally delayed claim accompanied by the reference, surcharge under 37 CFR 1.17(t), and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes specify use only for utility/plant applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, and conditions when not to use the paragraph (e.g., when the reference was previously submitted within time but not in first sentence or ADS yet recognized on filing receipt). Provides mailing address for petitions (Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority (35 U.S.C. 119) timing and content requirements (37 CFR 1.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for foreign priority must be presented during the pendency of the application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application (except designs and pre-Nov 29, 2000 filings). The claim must identify the foreign application by number, country/authority, and filing date. The claim and the certified copy of the foreign application must, in any event, be filed before the patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1) and (2). For national-stage applications, follow PCT time limits. If claim or certified copy is filed after issue fee is paid, processing fee under §1.17(i) is required and patent will not include priority unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and §1.323.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for right of priority to a foreign filing (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for claiming benefit of a prior foreign filing include: (A) foreign filing in a country affording similar privileges or a WTO member; (B) same applicant/inventor (or legal representative/assigns); (C) filed within 12 months from the earliest foreign filing date (6 months for designs); (D) foreign application must be for the same invention; (E)-(F) timing rules for U.S. and national-stage applications (four months/16 months or PCT limits); (G) inventor's-certificate handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes statutory and regulatory conditions (35 U.S.C. 119 and 37 CFR 1.55). Examiner may require certified copies, translations, or earlier filing of the certified copy where necessary (interference, overcoming reference, examiner's discretion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring earlier filing of priority claim or certified copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require that the claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application be filed earlier than the standard time limits when: (i) the application becomes involved in an interference; (ii) necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (iii) when deemed necessary by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is required under these circumstances, it must be filed together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate (37 CFR 1.55(a)(3) and (4)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation exceptions for foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An English language translation of a non-English-language foreign application is not required except when: (A) the application is involved in an interference; (B) necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (C) when specifically required by the examiner. If required, must be filed together with a statement that the translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 CFR 1.55(a)(4)(i) and (ii). Examiner may invoke this when translation is necessary for examination or for establishing priority in contested proceedings.
